reasons.A: Sustained long, clause-laden sentences with semicolon balancing and measured hedges ('arguably', 'it would be unfair') closest to the passage's formal, deliberative movement and two-to-three long-paragraph build.
reasons.B: Long stacked sentences, semicolons and a rhetorical question fit the author, but opening on the question and closing with a detached one-line paragraph make the structure more rhetorical than the passage.
reasons.C: Dashes and earnest hedging suit the author, but more short declarative sentences ('The warning is sound.') and four tidy paragraphs break the passage's long unbroken rhythm.
reasons.D: Short punchy sentences, second-person 'you', many one-idea paragraphs and a leadership-advice close read as plain modern blog prose, far from the author's formal, hedged periodic style.
